It may make sense to add a 'TESTED:' section to the bottom of the commit message. 

If I want to test this on my own machine, what's an example configuration I could use in entity-manager, and what should I look for to tell that it's working?

(you can surround large chunks of copy/pasted data that would normally break git commit message formatting and result with ''' marks if needed)

where's the code removing stale symlinks?


where's the check that the mux names and channel names are unique?


device and bus numbers not in the device tree can be reused after a parent unbind and the order is not preserved.

I did find code in FRU device with an inotify watch but it's not creating files or links so there's nothing to clean up.  that's the only other reference to "/dev" I found in a GitHub search of this repository (search pattern was `/dev[^i]/` ignoring a few false positives).


`libudev` can at least report when devices are removed.  it supports filters on the monitor for example the subsystem (i2c).
We still need to remember what was created to remove them, or rebuild or validate the directory on reload.  

udev would manage such symlinks if we told it what to create. libudev however it's purely reporting what's been decided by the udev rules from the kernel reporting netlink.

instead we'd need entries in udev rules (which this project is mostly trying to avoid from my observations) but we might be able to create a program involved by a rule that replies with the desired symlink creation.   I don't know what it'd take to have udev reprocess a device after it was matched to our inventory tree.   It can probably triggered with udevadm coldplug support.
while it's possible probably complex.

I'd be ok with something that looked for the target removal and unlink the symlink and directory created and some uniquenes checking.   (is the name supposed to include something from the instance like plug location?)
Checking for stale symlinks is in: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/entity-manager/+/80430
what is the purpose of this block? Try for 2nd time?

re-read the commit message a bit - looks like this is meant to retry after MUX is loaded and logic bus is available. I think we want make that more clear in the code either with some comments and/or function and variable names. 
Also i would expect this to be an iterative process as we can have mux behind a mux.

There is an iterative process when there are nested muxes with the creation of a new DeviceConfig object that attempts to be bound if a mux is detected to be connected behind the mux whose logical buses were identified (see linkMux and loadOverlays functions)
Hi @jonico.eustaquio@fii-na.com. I have not had a chance to test this yet but have some initial comments.
Would `DeviceConfig` objects then need to have `MuxChannel`/`ChannelName` added to it so that it can be compared against the muxMap?
Will `linkMux` be called when `buildDevice` is triggered as a retry?
Yes, `linkMux` will be called as long as `buildDevice` succeeds
You should compare `ec` against `file_exists` instead - https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/header/system_error.html.
Done
Done

Should "Bus" be looked for first to exclude entities that have already been linked before parsing more into MuxChannel?

I wonder if "MuxChannel" should be kept after "Bus" is filled? Because in the schema, "Bus" and "MuxChannel" can't exist together. After the linkMux job is done, MuxChannel is not useful anymore.

I don't think "MuxChannel" needs to be removed once "Bus" is inserted. The schema shows that they can't exist together as part of the user's configurations, but having the "Bus" be inserted by entity-manager after processing the configuration should be fine.

Maybe that would simplify the control flow as `linkMux` then only needs one branch in case the parsing function fails.
